summary: The token offer: {powerful officeholder} brings your group an offer: a token share of what it is fighting for, if it stops fighting.
realLife: In 1964 the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party challenged the all-white state delegation at the national convention. Senator Hubert Humphrey brought an offer of two seats; the group refused, and was seated four years later.
gates: You belong to a group challenging the party's slate or rules.
A party convention or committee meeting is on the calendar.
weights: How strong your group is on the record.
choices: refuse it and keep the challenge going
counter with a demand of your own

branches.then: Before the offer you speak to the committee, one part at a time, and how it goes changes the offer.
If you take it, the hard-liners blame you; some leave, and one runs against you later.
If you held out, the next convention seats your group in full, and {powerful officeholder} has to greet you.
